906 ## Topic 4 — Pulumi and Serverless Framework in CI 907 908 Accessed 2026-11-08. Sources and how they were read (all **local check**, HTTP 200): 909 - **Pulumi docs:** the raw Markdown that pulumi.com serves at `/index.md`. Links point to the 910 canonical URL each page declares. 911 - **Serverless Framework v4 docs:** read from the official repository `serverless/serverless` 912 (`docs/sf/…` on `main`), plus its GitHub release notes. Links point to the docs site. 913 - **AWS CloudFormation pages:** raw `.md` from docs.aws.amazon.com. 914 915 **Papaya facts that are unknown:** whether Pulumi uses Pulumi Cloud or a DIY (S3) backend, and 916 which Pulumi Cloud edition. The same goes for the Serverless Framework major version and 917 subscription. Each row says when it depends on one of these. 918 919 ### 4.1 Pulumi: preview and up in CI 920 921 | # | Finding | Marker | Source | 922 |---|---|---|---| 923 | 4.1.1 | `pulumi preview` flags relevant to CI: `--diff`, `--json`, `--expect-no-changes` ("Return an error if any changes are proposed"), `--policy-pack`, `--refresh`, `--target`, and `--save-plan` (marked **[PREVIEW]**). `--show-secrets` defaults to false; "if used with `--save-plan` the secrets will also be shown in the plan file". | ✅ | [pulumi preview](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_preview/) | 924 | 4.1.2 | `pulumi up` flags: `--yes` ("Automatically approve and perform the update after previewing it"), `--skip-preview`, `--plan ` (**[EXPERIMENTAL]**: "will not perform operations that exceed its plan"), `--strict` (**[EXPERIMENTAL]**: generate a plan during preview and constrain the update to it), and `--expect-no-changes`, where "This check happens after the update is applied". | ✅ | [pulumi up](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_up/) | 925 | 4.1.3 | **Update plans:** "`pulumi preview --save-plan=plan.json`" then "`pulumi up --plan=plan.json`" constrains the update "to allow only the changes described in the plan". The docs say this "may be useful in organizations with strict approval processes".
Limits:
- Values unknown at preview time are recorded as `unknown`.
- Resources created inside an `apply` are not recorded, which causes an error at update time.
- Providers with unknown inputs are not fully diffed.
- The docs say the plan is "not as strong a guarantee as to what the program will do".
- The plan file format "is currently experimental and subject to change". | ✅ | [Update plans](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/operations/stack-management/update-plans/) | 926 | 4.1.4 | Pulumi's GitHub Actions guide uses `pulumi/actions` (`command: preview` on `pull_request`, `up` on push), with optional PR comments. It recommends **OIDC token exchange** through `pulumi/auth-actions` ("no stored secret") over a stored `PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN`. Cloud credentials come either from Pulumi ESC or directly from cloud OIDC, for example `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials`. The guide assumes Pulumi Cloud, but "Pulumi Cloud isn't required to run Pulumi in CI/CD". | ✅ | [GitHub Actions](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/using-pulumi/continuous-delivery/github-actions/) | 927 | 4.1.5 | **Pulumi Cloud OIDC trust for GitHub:**
- Organization tokens are available on the Essentials, Pro and Enterprise editions; team and personal tokens also exist.
- The example subject is `repo:/:*`. That is the old `sub` format with a wildcard, which matches any branch, PR or environment.
- Setting it up requires being "an admin of your Pulumi organization". | ✅ | [OIDC: GitHub](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/pulumi-cloud/access-management/oidc/client/github/) | 928 929 ### 4.2 Pulumi: policy as code ("CrossGuard") 930 931 | # | Finding | Marker | Source | 932 |---|---|---|---| 933 | 4.2.1 | **Naming:** the current docs call the product **"Pulumi Policies"**. "CrossGuard" does not appear in any Pulumi page downloaded (`grep -c -i crossguard` = 0, **local check**). I assume this is the same product renamed (⚠️). | ✅ (name) / ⚠️ (rename) | [Policy as code](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/) | 934 | 4.2.2 | Policies are written in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python or OPA Rego. They run as analyzer plugins during `pulumi preview` and `pulumi up`, "before anything changes in your cloud provider", and "a violation of a mandatory policy stops the deployment". The enforcement levels are `advisory`, `mandatory`, `remediate` and `disabled`. | ✅ | [Policy as code](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/), [Policy packs](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/policy-packs/) | 935 | 4.2.3 | **Two ways to enforce:**
- **Open source, local:** the job runs `--policy-pack `. This works "with any backend, including the self-managed backend". The pack must be on disk where Pulumi runs.
- **Pulumi Cloud** (Essentials, Pro and Enterprise): policy groups apply packs to stacks "without passing `--policy-pack` on each command", and the CLI downloads them automatically. Pre-built compliance packs (CIS, HITRUST, ISO 27001, NIST, PCI DSS) are on Enterprise. Audit policies over discovered resources need Pulumi Cloud. | ✅ | [Policy as code](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/) | 936 | 4.2.4 | **Inference:** with local enforcement, the policy flag lives in the CI workflow. A PR that edits the workflow can drop it, so it is only as strong as CODEOWNERS on `.github/` (3.2.8). Enforcement through Cloud policy groups does not depend on the flag. Whether a CLI user can opt out of Cloud-enforced packs was not found in the pages read (⚠️). | ⚠️ inference | — | 937 938 ### 4.3 Pulumi: drift, state and secrets 939 940 | # | Finding | Marker | Source | 941 |---|---|---|---| 942 | 4.3.1 | Pulumi does **not** refresh automatically: preview and up compare the program with the **recorded** state. Out-of-band changes are not seen, and "may produce unexpected results including overwriting them". `pulumi refresh` updates only state. `--refresh` on preview or up refreshes first. | ✅ | [State and backends](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/concepts/state-and-backends/) | 943 | 4.3.2 | **Drift detection:**
- **Scheduled (Pulumi Cloud Deployments):** available on the **Pro and Enterprise** editions. It runs a refresh periodically and alerts, or optionally remediates.
- **From the CLI:** "`pulumi refresh --preview-only`", which a job on any backend can run on a schedule (inference). | ✅ | [Drift detection and remediation](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/deployments/concepts/drift/), [State and backends](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/concepts/state-and-backends/) | 944 | 4.3.3 | **Backends:** Pulumi Cloud, the default, or **DIY**: S3, Azure Blob, GCS, an S3-compatible store, PostgreSQL or local disk. "DIY backends include built-in state locking and history tracking". The S3 backend needs `s3:ListBucket`, `GetObject`, `PutObject` and `DeleteObject` under `.pulumi/` "across the full stack lifecycle", including `pulumi preview`. DIY backends "cannot transparently recover from certain kinds of partial failures". | ✅ | [State and backends](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/concepts/state-and-backends/), [Using a DIY backend](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/) | 945 | 4.3.4 | **Secrets:** Pulumi tracks secrets transitively and encrypts them in state "no matter which backend you've chosen". With Pulumi Cloud the default key is a per-stack key managed by Pulumi Cloud. Alternatives are set with `--secrets-provider` at stack init: `awskms`, `azurekeyvault`, `gcpkms`, `hashivault`, `passphrase`. Config values are plain text unless set with `--secret`. | ✅ | [Secrets](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/concepts/secrets/), [State and backends](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/concepts/state-and-backends/) | 946 | 4.3.5 | **Pulumi Cloud audit logs:** Pro and Enterprise editions. Automatic export to S3 or Microsoft Sentinel: Enterprise only. | ✅ | [Audit logs](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/administration/concepts/audit-logs/) | 947 948 ### 4.4 Serverless Framework (v4) in CI 949 950 | # | Finding | Marker | Source | 951 |---|---|---|---| 952 | 4.4.1 | `serverless deploy` turns `serverless.yml` into **one CloudFormation stack** and updates it. Since v4 the default `deploymentMethod` is `direct`, and `changesets` is opt-in. **State is the CloudFormation stack plus the deployment bucket.** Compose services also keep state in S3, located through an SSM parameter in `us-east-1`. | ✅ | [Deploying](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/deploying), [serverless.yml reference](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/serverless.yml), [State](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/guides/state) | 953 | 4.4.2 | **Preview:** `serverless diff` shows Lambda code changes and a structured CloudFormation template diff (resources, **IAM statements**, security groups, outputs), with "(requires replacement)" markers, `--json` "for CI consumption", and `--package` to diff an already built package. It was **added in sf-core 4.37.0 (2026-05-27)**, per the release notes; older v4 versions do not have it. | ✅ | [diff](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/cli-reference/diff), [release sf-core@4.37.0](https://github.com/serverless/serverless/releases/tag/sf-core%404.37.0) | 954 | 4.4.3 | **Build once, deploy that artifact:** `serverless package` then `serverless deploy --package `, which "bypasses the package step and uses the existing package". | ✅ | [Deploying](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/deploying) | 955 | 4.4.4 | **`serverless deploy function`** "does not touch your AWS CloudFormation Stack. Instead, it simply overwrites the zip file of the current function". The docs present it as a fast development path. | ✅ | [Deploying](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/deploying) | 956 | 4.4.5 | `provider.iam.deploymentRole`: "ARN of an IAM role for CloudFormation service. If specified, CloudFormation uses the role's credentials". AWS warns: "It is not possible to remove a service role attached to a stack after the stack is created". Also: "Other users that have permissions to perform operations on this stack are able to use this role, regardless of whether those users have the `iam:PassRole` permission". Other relevant options: `stackPolicy`, `rollbackConfiguration`, `disableRollback` (non-prod). | ✅ | [serverless.yml reference](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/serverless.yml), [CloudFormation service role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-iam-servicerole.html) | 957 | 4.4.6 | **Drift:** Serverless has no drift command. `serverless reconcile` is about billing ("reconciles your org's list of billable instances"). CloudFormation drift detection applies to the stack, with limits: it covers only resource types that support it (others are `NOT_CHECKED`), and only "property values that are explicitly set", not defaults. | ✅ | [reconcile](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/cli-reference/reconcile), [CloudFormation drift detection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-stack-drift.html) | 958 | 4.4.7 | **Secrets:** `${ssm:…}` variables, and Secrets Manager through `ssm:/aws/reference/secretsmanager/…`. They are resolved with "the deployment (provider) AWS credentials". SecureString values are decrypted unless `noDecrypt` is set. Whether resolved values then sit in plain text in the CloudFormation template, for example as Lambda environment variables, is not stated on the page read (⚠️). | ✅ / ⚠️ | [Variables: SSM & Secrets Manager](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/guides/variables/aws/ssm) | 959 | 4.4.8 | **Licensing and authentication:** "Starting with Version 4, authentication is required for all users". Organizations with "annual revenue exceeding $2M USD" need a subscription. In CI, **License Keys** "do not offer access control or permissions", have "No Expiration" (rotate them as a best practice), and disable Dashboard access. | ✅ | [License keys](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/guides/license-keys), [Upgrading to v4](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/guides/upgrading-v4) | 960 961 ### 4.5 Mapping to Terraform / OpenTofu (one sentence) 962 963 In Terraform/OpenTofu terms: 964 - `pulumi preview` ≈ `plan`; 965 - `pulumi up` ≈ `apply`; 966 - an update plan ≈ applying a saved plan file; 967 - `pulumi refresh` ≈ a refresh-only plan; 968 - Pulumi Policies ≈ Sentinel/OPA; 969 - Pulumi Cloud or a DIY S3 backend ≈ HCP Terraform or an S3 backend. 970 971 So the controls below carry over to Terraform/OpenTofu shops. Marker: 📖 for the Pulumi side and 972 the existence of Sentinel ([Pulumi vs Terraform](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/comparisons/terraform/)); 973 ⚠️ for the exact Terraform/OpenTofu command names, whose docs were not read this session. 974 975 ### 4.6 What this means for Papaya (inferences — to be used in the design) 976 977 These are my conclusions from the findings above, not documented facts: 978 979 1. **Make "what the reviewer approved" equal "what gets applied".** 980 - **Pulumi:** run `pulumi preview --diff` with policies on the PR, and post it as a PR comment 981 for the reviewer. On merge, run `pulumi up` from `main` under the `production` environment 982 (3.6 #1). 983 - **Option, `--save-plan` / `up --plan`:** it ties the apply to the reviewed preview, but it is 984 preview/experimental and has documented gaps (4.1.3). Treat it as a guard, not as proof. 985 Plan files can carry secrets if `--show-secrets` is used (4.1.1). 986 - **Serverless:** `sls diff --json` on the PR (requires ≥ 4.37.0, 4.4.2); on merge, 987 `package` then `deploy --package` of the same artifact (4.4.3). 988 2. **A PR preview needs prod read access, and runs the PR's code.** 989 - `pulumi preview` executes the program, and with an S3 backend it also writes lock objects 990 (4.3.3). `sls diff` packages the service and reads the deployed stack (4.4.2). 991 - So a PR job that previews prod needs a **separate read-only "plan" role**. That role must 992 still be treated as exposed to PR code: anyone who can open a PR can run code with it. 993 - Under GĐ-9 / 1.11, the plan role must not have data-plane reads on PHI stores. 994 - The apply role exists only for `main` + `production`. 995 - This is a tension with 3.6 #1 ("only `main` gets prod credentials"). It is resolved by having 996 two roles with different trust: a `pr-preview` environment or `pull_request` sub for the plan 997 role, and `environment:production` for the apply role. 998 3. **Close the bypass paths in the tools themselves:** 999 - `serverless deploy function` skips CloudFormation and its review (4.4.4). Deny it in prod via 1000 IAM (`lambda:UpdateFunctionCode` only for the CloudFormation deployment role, 4.4.5, ⚠️ 1001 design). 1002 - Use a least-privilege `deploymentRole`. It cannot be removed later, and anyone who may 1003 operate the stack can use it (4.4.5). 1004 - Pulumi `--target` and `--skip-preview` should not appear in prod workflows (4.1.1, 4.1.2). 1005 4. **Policy as code where the agent can't switch it off.** 1006 - Prefer Pulumi Cloud policy groups (Essentials+) if Papaya is on Pulumi Cloud. 1007 - Otherwise use `--policy-pack` in a CODEOWNERS-protected reusable workflow (4.2.3, 4.2.4). 1008 - For Serverless, the CloudFormation template from `sls package` can be checked by a CI policy 1009 tool (⚠️ tool not researched). Plus IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on changed 1010 policies (2.8.1). 1011 5. **Drift is a compliance signal, because it means an unreviewed change happened.** 1012 - **Pulumi:** scheduled `pulumi refresh --preview-only` or `preview --expect-no-changes` in CI 1013 (any backend), or Pulumi Cloud drift detection (Pro+) (4.3.2). 1014 - **Serverless:** scheduled CloudFormation drift detection, with its coverage limits (4.4.6). 1015 - Every drift finding should map to a CloudTrail actor (2.5) and an incident or ticket. 1016 6. **State and secrets:** 1017 - Pulumi state and Serverless state buckets are **prod-sensitive stores**. They hold encrypted 1018 secrets and resource details. Restrict them to the deploy roles (4.3.3, 4.4.1). 1019 - Use a cloud-KMS secrets provider (`awskms`) if Papaya uses a DIY backend (4.3.4). 1020 - Serverless secrets should be resolved at runtime, not baked into templates (⚠️ 4.4.7). 1021 - The Serverless License Key is a long-lived CI secret with no access control (4.4.8). Keep it 1022 in the environment, not repository secrets (3.5.3b). 1023 1024 ### 4.7 Open items (Topic 4) 1025 1026 - [ ] ⚠️ Papaya's Pulumi backend (Pulumi Cloud vs DIY S3) and edition; Serverless version 1027 (≥ 4.37.0 for `diff`?) and subscription. 1028 - [ ] ⚠️ Can a CLI user bypass Pulumi Cloud policy-group enforcement (4.2.4)? 1029 - [ ] ⚠️ Do Serverless-resolved SSM/Secrets Manager values end up in plain text in the 1030 CloudFormation template (4.4.7)? 1031 - [ ] ⚠️ The exact Terraform/OpenTofu command names (4.5); CI policy tools for CloudFormation 1032 templates (4.6 #4). 1033 1034 ### 4.8 Review log (Topic 4) 1035 1036 (to be filled after the independent review) 1037

> **Note:** This guide assumes [Pulumi Cloud](/docs/pulumi-cloud/) as your backend. Pulumi Cloud isn't required to run Pulumi in CI/CD — Pulumi also supports [self-managed backends](/docs/iac/concepts/state-and-backends/) — but the access token, OIDC, and ESC features described here are specific to Pulumi Cloud.
Your workflow authenticates to Pulumi Cloud with a single [Pulumi access token](/docs/administration/concepts/access-tokens/), supplied through the `PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN` environment variable. Prefer an [organization or team token](/docs/administration/concepts/access-tokens/#creating-an-organization-access-token) over a personal token so the workflow's identity isn't tied to an individual.
Pair it with [`pulumi/esc-action`](https://github.com/pulumi/esc-action) to pull cloud credentials, secrets, and configuration from a [Pulumi ESC](/docs/esc/) environment. This is the recommended way to provide cloud credentials in GitHub Actions because it's:
To configure OIDC directly between GitHub Actions and a cloud provider without ESC — for example, with `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` and a `role-to-assume` input — follow that provider's GitHub Actions OIDC guide. This approach is provider-specific: each cloud requires its own trust relationship, whereas ESC configures that trust once and reuses it everywhere.
When pull requests stack up or commits land faster than a workflow finishes, runs accumulate. [Concurrency groups](https://docs.github.com/actions/using-jobs/using-concurrency) bound how many run at once. Letting two runs reach the same stack at once causes one to fail with an [update conflict](/docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/), so a concurrency group on your deployment jobs is worth setting up before you hit one.

For **pull request previews**, key the group to the pull request and cancel superseded runs so reviewers always see the result of the latest commit:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: pulumi-pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

For **deployments**, use a shared group *without* `cancel-in-progress` so updates queue instead of being dropped — canceling a deployment mid-run can leave infrastructure half-applied:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: pulumi-deploy
```

`concurrency` is a top-level workflow key, placed alongside `on` and `jobs`. You can also scope it to a single job when a workflow contains jobs with different concurrency needs.

### Authorization policy

1. Select the issuer name.

## Refreshing state

Pulumi's state records what your infrastructure looked like after the last `pulumi up` or `pulumi refresh`. When you run `pulumi preview` or `pulumi up`, Pulumi compares this recorded state against the configuration declared in your program to determine which changes need to be made. It does not query each resource directly from your cloud provider on every run.

This means that if someone modifies a resource _outside_ of Pulumi (by editing it in the cloud provider's console, applying a change with a provider CLI, or by some other out-of-band means), that change is not automatically reflected in Pulumi's state. The next `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview` will not account for those changes, and may produce unexpected results including overwriting them.

### Why Pulumi does not refresh automatically

Pulumi intentionally does not refresh state before every operation, for several reasons:

- **Performance**: Querying every resource's live state from the cloud provider can be slow, particularly for large stacks with hundreds or thousands of resources. Doing this implicitly on every `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview` would add significant latency for the typical case where no out-of-band changes have been made.
- **Explicit control**: Pulumi treats your program as the source of truth for desired state. Automatically reconciling out-of-band changes before each operation could cause your program and your actual infrastructure to diverge silently, or could cause Pulumi to preserve changes you intended to overwrite.
- **Predictability**: Keeping refresh explicit means you decide when and whether to incorporate external changes versus overwrite them, giving you confidence about what each `pulumi up` will do.

### Running `pulumi refresh`


Pulumi state is usually stored in a transactional snapshot called a _checkpoint_. Pulumi records checkpoints early and often as it executes so that Pulumi can operate reliably, the way database transactions do. The basic functions of state allow Pulumi to diff your program's goal state against the last known update, recover from failure, and destroy resources accurately to clean up afterwards. The checkpoint format augments this with additional failure recovery capabilities in the face of partia

The Pulumi Cloud backend records every checkpoint through a transactional API, making it possible to transparently recover from unusual failure scenarios such as network interruptions during updates. DIY backends also maintain checkpoint history (in the `.pulumi/history/` directory), but because they are fundamentally limited by the non-transactional protocols of blob storage, they cannot transparently recover from certain kinds of partial failures (read more about how Pulumi Cloud addresses thi

To synchronize Pulumi's recorded state with the actual state of your cloud resources, run:

```sh
$ pulumi refresh
```

This command queries each resource in your stack from the cloud provider and updates Pulumi's state file to reflect any differences. If a resource has been deleted outside of Pulumi, Pulumi removes it from the state. If properties have changed, Pulumi updates the state to match.

`pulumi refresh` updates only the state. It does not modify your Pulumi program or apply any changes to your infrastructure. If you want to preserve external changes going forward, you also need to update your program to reflect the new configuration; otherwise, the next `pulumi up` will attempt to 

Run `pulumi refresh` when:

- Resources have been modified or deleted outside of Pulumi, such as through the cloud console or another tool.
- You are troubleshooting unexpected diffs during a `pulumi preview` and suspect the state may be stale.
- You want to verify that Pulumi's recorded state accurately reflects reality before running a `pulumi destroy`.

### Refreshing as part of an update

To refresh state and then apply your program's desired state in a single step, pass the `--refresh` flag to `pulumi up`:

```sh
$ pulumi up --refresh
```

# AWS - Diff

The `sls diff` command shows the difference between the CloudFormation template generated from your current configuration and the stack currently deployed in AWS. It is useful for reviewing changes before running `sls deploy`, especially in CI / PR-review workflows.

```bash
serverless diff
```

Two orthogonal signals are surfaced:

1. **Function Code changes** — per-function comparison of the locally-packaged zip against each Lambda's `CodeSha256` in AWS. Tells you which functions will have their code redeployed. A service with [web apps](../guide/web-apps.md) also gets a **Web App Code** section, which lists the web apps wh
2. **CloudFormation template diff** — a structured diff of resources, IAM statements, security groups, parameters, outputs, and other top-level template sections. Tells you what CloudFormation will change.

By default, the service is packaged first so the local template reflects the current configuration on disk. If you already have a packaged artifact directory (for example, from a previous CI step), pass `--package <path>` to use it directly and skip repackaging.

## Options

- `--stage` or `-s` The service stage to diff against. Defaults to the stage from `serverless.yml` or `dev`.
- `--region` or `-r` The service region to diff against.
- `--aws-profile` The AWS profile to use.
- `--stack` CloudFormation stack name override.
- `--package` or `-p` Path to an existing package directory to diff against. Skips the auto-package step when set.
- `--json` Output the diff in JSON format. Suitable for CI consumption.

## Provided lifecycle events

- `diff:diff`

## Examples

### No changes against the deployed stack

```text
Packaging "my-service" for stage "dev" (us-east-1)
No function code changes
No infrastructure changes against the deployed stack
✔ Service packaged (2s)
```

### Configuration-only change

You bumped a Lambda's memory but did not edit any handler files:

```text
Function Code
(no entries — handler bytes are unchanged)

Resources
[~] AWS::Lambda::Function HelloLambdaFunction
 └─ [~] MemorySize
     ├─ [-] 1024
     └─ [+] 2048

Resources: 1 to create, 1 to update, 1 to remove
```

The `Function Code` section is empty (or absent) because no handler files changed. The structured diff shows the property change and the matching Lambda Version churn that CloudFormation will perform.

## Exit code

`sls diff` exits `0` unless an unrecoverable error occurs (for example, AWS credentials are missing or the local template could not be read). Differences against the deployed stack do not cause a non-zero exit code — the command is informational.

## Behavior notes

- The structured diff applies the same template normalization the framework uses internally to decide whether a deploy is necessary, so artifact-key churn that the framework considers meaningless does not appear in the diff.
- The `Function Code` section is the truthful "did handler code change?" signal — it compares zip hashes against AWS Lambda's `CodeSha256`. It is independent of the template-level diff below it.
- The `Web App Code` section compares the content-derived name of each web app's zip in the local template with the one in the deployed stack's template, so it needs no AWS calls beyond reading that template.
- Custom configuration filenames (`--config my-service.yml`) are supported.

# AWS - Deploy Function

The `sls deploy function` command deploys an individual function without AWS CloudFormation. This command simply swaps out the zip file that your CloudFormation stack is pointing toward. This is a much faster way of deploying changes in code.

```bash
serverless deploy function -f functionName
```

**Note:** This command **now** deploys both function configuration and code by
default. Just as before, this puts your function in an inconsistent state that
is out of sync with your CloudFormation stack. Use this for faster development
cycles and not production deployments. A later `serverless deploy` does not
undo a configuration change made this way: CloudFormation changes only what
differs from the template it deployed last, and when nothing else changed,
the deploy is skipped. To put the function back, run
`serverless deploy function` again from the configuration you want. With
`codeStorageMode: reference`, this command updates the function using
Lambda-managed storage; the next `serverless deploy` restores reference mode.

`deploy function` deploys functions only. [Web apps](../guide/web-apps.md) deploy with `serverless deploy`; given a web app's name, the command stops with `"<name>" is a web app. Deploy it with serverless deploy.`

## Options

- `--function` or `-f` The name of the function which should be deployed
- `--stage` or `-s` The stage in your service that you want to deploy to.
- `--region` or `-r` The region in that stage that you want to deploy to.
- `--aws-profile` The AWS profile you want to use.
- `--update-config` or `-u` Pushes ONLY Lambda-level configuration changes e.g. handler, timeout or memorySize

## Examples

### Deployment without stage and region options

```bash
serverless deploy function --function helloWorld
```

When you specify a service role, CloudFormation always uses that role for all operations that are performed on that stack. It is not possible to remove a service role attached to a stack after the stack is created. Other users that have permissions to perform operations on this stack are able to use this role, regardless of whether those users have the `iam:PassRole` permission or not. If the role includes permissions that the user shouldn't have, you can unintentionally escalate a user's permissions. Ensure that the role grants least privilege. For more information, see [Apply least-privilege permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html#grant-least-privilege) in the *IAM User Guide*.    foo: bar

### 3.6 What this means for Papaya (inferences — to be used in the design)

These are my conclusions from the findings above, not documented facts:

1. **The GitHub plan decides where the "named human approved it" gate can sit.**
   - **On Enterprise Cloud:** a `production` environment with required reviewers, prevent
     self-review, no admin bypass, and deployment branches = `main` (3.1.1–3.1.4). The approval
     is per deployment job and logged as `workflows.approve_workflow_job` (3.5.6).
   - **On Team:** environments have **no approval gate** on a private repo (3.1.2). The gate must
     be the **PR merge to `main`**, enforced by:
     - rulesets: PR required, ≥1–2 approvals, code-owner review, path-based team reviewers for
       `infra/**` and `.github/**`, dismiss stale approvals, last-push approval, an empty bypass
       list (3.2.2–3.2.4);
     - the `production` environment restricted to `main` (3.1.3).
   - **Prerequisite on both plans: the branch rule alone does not mean "only merged, approved
     code reaches prod".** Every workflow on `main` passes a "main only" rule, whatever its trigger
     (3.4.5c). So all of the following must also hold:
     - only reviewed deploy workflows may reference `production`, enforced by CODEOWNERS on
       `.github/workflows` and a CI check;
     - deploy workflows take no ref or SHA input, and deploy the commit they run on;
     - no `production` job runs on `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run`.
       A `schedule` deploy of the current `main` commit is acceptable only if it deploys that
       commit and takes no input;
     - preferably, the `sub` claim is pinned to the reusable deploy workflow (`job_workflow_ref`,
       3.4.5).

     Under these conditions, merge approval equals deploy approval on Team.
   - **Admins remain a gap.** Admins and holders of "edit repository rules" can edit rulesets,
     environments and the OIDC `sub` customisation. This is mostly logged, not prevented (3.1.4,
     3.2.2, 3.4.5). So: few admins, periodic access review, and alerts on `repository_ruleset.update`,
     `environment.update_protection_rule`, `environment.remove_protection_rule`,
     `environment.delete` and `protected_branch.policy_override`.
   - **UI changes to the branch policy may not be audited** (⚠️, 3.1.4). A deleted
     `production` environment is likely recreated without protection by the next workflow
     that references it. The deletion itself is logged (⚠️ inference, 3.1.4). So a scheduled
     job should also compare the live environment configuration with the expected one, as
     drift detection (⚠️: the REST endpoint was not researched).
   - **GĐ-5 holds only on Enterprise.** It should go back to the framing as a correction and an
     open question for Papaya.
2. **OIDC trust must pin the repository, the gate and, where possible, the workflow** (3.4.2–3.4.5c):
   - **AWS:** prod roles trust only `repo:<org>/<repo>:environment:production`, in the repo's
     `sub` format (3.4.4). Ideally a customised `sub` includes `job_workflow_ref`, because AWS
     cannot test other claims (3.4.5).
   - **GCP:** the attribute condition must restrict to the GitHub organization (required by
     Google). It can also test `job_workflow_ref`, `ref` and `event_name` directly (3.4.5b).
   - **Non-prod:** roles trust a separate environment.
   - **Secrets:** prod credentials never live in repository secrets, because anyone with write
     access can read those (3.5.3b). This removes the long-lived AWS keys from the brief (P5).
3. **Agent-authored PRs need one more rule than human PRs** (3.3.4). Opening PRs with the
   engineer's own identity keeps GitHub's built-in author rule. App-authored PRs need 2 approvals
   or a custom check whose source app is pinned. "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull
   requests" stays **off** (3.3.3).
4. **CI agents and policy files:** on standard GitHub-hosted runners, an agent with shell access
   has root, so Claude Code managed settings written in the job are advisory (3.5.1, closes the
   Topic 1 question). The real limits for a CI agent are:
   - the job's `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions (3.5.3);
   - **no** `environment: production` in any agent workflow, so it gets no prod OIDC trust
     (3.4.5c);
   - the base-branch config restore in `claude-code-action` (1.7.9).

   Self-hosted runners would allow a root-owned policy, but bring persistence risks (3.5.2).
5. **Supply chain of CI itself:**
   - Workflow lockfile or SHA pinning, enforced by org policy (3.5.5).
   - CODEOWNERS on `.github/` (3.2.8), plus CI validation of the CODEOWNERS file, because invalid
     lines fail silently (3.2.7).
   - Restricted default `GITHUB_TOKEN` (3.5.3); no `pull_request_target` with checkout (3.5.4).
6. **Audit retention gap:** the org audit log keeps 180 days (3.5.6). ISO 27001 and HIPAA evidence
   needs longer, so it must be exported periodically (JSON or CSV, within the export limits, ✅)
   or streamed (⚠️ not researched; may be Enterprise-only).

### Required permissions

The S3 backend reads and writes state, lock, history, and metadata objects under the bucket's `.pulumi` prefix. Across the full stack lifecycle—`pulumi new`/`pulumi stack init`, `pulumi preview`, `pulumi up`, `pulumi refresh`, `pulumi destroy`, and `pulumi stack rm`—it needs exactly four S3 actions, and no more:

- `s3:ListBucket` to enumerate stacks and locks.
- `s3:GetObject` to read `meta.yaml`, stack state, and lock files.
- `s3:PutObject` to write stack state, history, and lock files.
- `s3:DeleteObject` to release locks and remove stacks.

Note that `s3:ListBucket` is a bucket-level action, so it must be granted on the bucket ARN (`arn:aws:s3:::<bucket-name>`), while the object-level actions are granted on the objects within it (`arn:aws:s3:::<bucket-name>/*`). {
$ pulumi login azblob://<container-path>
```

Since Serverless Framework v4, deployments are by default done using [CloudFormation direct deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-updating-stacks-direct.html). This is the recommended approach for most users.

If you want to instead use [CloudFormation change sets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-updating-stacks-changesets.html), you can enable it via the `deploymentMethod` option:

```yml
provider:
  name: aws
  deploymentMethod: changesets
```

SLS_AWS_SDK=3 serverless deploy
```

Show a preview of updates to a stack's resources
## Synopsis
Show a preview of updates to a stack's resources.
This command displays a preview of the updates to an existing stack whose state is
represented by an existing state file. The new desired state is computed by running
a Pulumi program, and extracting all resource allocations from its resulting object graph.
These allocations are then compared against the existing state to determine what
operations must take place to achieve the desired state. No changes to the stack will
actually take place.
The program to run is loaded from the project in the current directory. Use the `-C` or
`--cwd` flag to use a different directory.
```
pulumi preview [url] [flags]
```

## Topic 4 — Pulumi and Serverless Framework in CI Accessed 2026-11-08. Sources and how they were read (all **local check**, HTTP 200): - **Pulumi docs:** the raw Markdown that pulumi.com serves at `/index.md`. Links point to the canonical URL each page declares. - **Serverless Framework v4 docs:** read from the official repository `serverless/serverless` (`docs/sf/…` on `main`), plus its GitHub release notes. Links point to the docs site. - **AWS CloudFormation pages:** raw `.md` from docs.aws.amazon.com. **Papaya facts that are unknown:** whether Pulumi uses Pulumi Cloud or a DIY (S3) backend, and which Pulumi Cloud edition. The same goes for the Serverless Framework major version and subscription. Each row says when it depends on one of these. ### 4.1 Pulumi: preview and up in CI | # | Finding | Marker | Source | |---|---|---|---| | 4.1.1 | `pulumi preview` flags relevant to CI: `--diff`, `--json`, `--expect-no-changes` ("Return an error if any changes are proposed"), `--policy-pack`, `--refresh`, `--target`, and `--save-plan` (marked **[PREVIEW]**). `--show-secrets` defaults to false; "if used with `--save-plan` the secrets will also be shown in the plan file". | ✅ | [pulumi preview](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_preview/) | | 4.1.2 | `pulumi up` flags: `--yes` ("Automatically approve and perform the update after previewing it"), `--skip-preview`, `--plan ` (**[EXPERIMENTAL]**: "will not perform operations that exceed its plan"), `--strict` (**[EXPERIMENTAL]**: generate a plan during preview and constrain the update to it), and `--expect-no-changes`, where "This check happens after the update is applied". | ✅ | [pulumi up](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_up/) | | 4.1.3 | **Update plans:** "`pulumi preview --save-plan=plan.json`" then "`pulumi up --plan=plan.json`" constrains the update "to allow only the changes described in the plan". The docs say this "may be useful in organizations with strict approval processes".
Limits:
- Values unknown at preview time are recorded as `unknown`.
- Resources created inside an `apply` are not recorded, which causes an error at update time.
- Providers with unknown inputs are not fully diffed.
- The docs say the plan is "not as strong a guarantee as to what the program will do".
- The plan file format "is currently experimental and subject to change". | ✅ | [Update plans](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/operations/stack-management/update-plans/) | | 4.1.4 | Pulumi's GitHub Actions guide uses `pulumi/actions` (`command: preview` on `pull_request`, `up` on push), with optional PR comments. It recommends **OIDC token exchange** through `pulumi/auth-actions` ("no stored secret") over a stored `PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN`. Cloud credentials come either from Pulumi ESC or directly from cloud OIDC, for example `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials`. The guide assumes Pulumi Cloud, but "Pulumi Cloud isn't required to run Pulumi in CI/CD". The guide calls ESC "the recommended way to provide cloud credentials". For deployments it advises "a shared group *without* `cancel-in-progress`" because "canceling a deployment mid-run can leave infrastructure half-applied". | ✅ | [GitHub Actions](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/github-actions/) | | 4.1.5 | **Pulumi Cloud OIDC trust for GitHub:**

22:| 4.1.5 | **Pulumi Cloud OIDC trust for GitHub:**
- Organization tokens are available on the Essentials, Pro and Enterprise editions.
- Team tokens are available on Pro and Enterprise. Personal tokens also exist.
- The example subject is `repo:/:*`. **Inference:** that is the old `sub` format (3.4.4) with a wildcard, which matches any branch, PR or environment.
- Whether the Pulumi policy can pin `environment:production` was not checked (⚠️).
- Setting it up requires being "an admin of your Pulumi organization". | ✅ / ⚠️ | [OIDC: GitHub](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/administration/guides/oidc-issuers/github/) | 31:| 4.2.4 | **Inference:**
- **Local enforcement:** the policy flag lives in the CI workflow. A PR that edits the workflow can drop it, so it is only as strong as CODEOWNERS on `.github/` (3.2.8).
- **PR preview:** policy packs run on "the machine that runs Pulumi", together with the PR's code. So in a PR preview a policy result is advice. The **enforcing** run is `up` on `main`.
- **Cloud policy groups:** they do not depend on the flag. But `pulumi policy disable` exists, so a Pulumi org admin can switch a policy off. Whether a CLI user can opt out was not found (⚠️).
- **`remediate`:** this level "fixes the resource automatically", so the deployed resource can differ from the code the reviewer read.

Status: ⚠️ inference; ✅ for the quotes. | ⚠️ inference / ✅ (quotes) | [Policy as code](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/), [Policy packs](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/policy-packs/), [Policy groups](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/discovery-governance/concepts/policy-as-code/policy-groups/) | 38:| 4.3.2 | **Drift detection:**
- **Scheduled (Pulumi Cloud Deployments):** available on the **Pro and Enterprise** editions. It needs the stack's "deployment settings", so Pulumi Cloud must hold credentials for the target. Optional **auto-remediation** "runs `pulumi up --refresh`". That is an unreviewed prod change.
- **From the CLI:** `pulumi refresh --preview-only` ("Only show a preview of the refresh"), which a job on any backend can run on a schedule (inference).
- The CLI drift guide (`/docs/iac/operations/stack-management/drift/`) was **not read** (⚠️). | ✅ / ⚠️ | [Drift detection and remediation](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/deployments/concepts/drift/), [pulumi refresh](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_refresh/) | 54:| 4.4.8 | **Licensing and authentication:** "Starting with Version 4, authentication is required for all users". Organizations with "annual revenue exceeding $2M USD" need a subscription. In CI, **License Keys** "do not offer access control or permissions", have "No Expiration" (rotate them as a best practice), and disable Dashboard access. "As of Serverless Framework version 4.4.19 you can store your License Key in AWS SSM Parameter Store", read with the deploy credentials. Inference: then no CI secret is needed. | ✅ / ⚠️ (inference) | [License keys](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/guides/license-keys), [Upgrading to v4](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/guides/upgrading-v4) | 55:| 4.4.9 | **Other paths that hold prod credentials, outside the GitHub gate:**
- **Pulumi ESC**, recommended by Pulumi for cloud credentials (4.1.4).
- **Pulumi Deployments:** Click to Deploy, schedules, drift runs. They need deployment settings (4.3.2).
- **Serverless Dashboard Providers** ("the easiest and simplest way" to connect to AWS with an IAM role). Credential *resolvers* only pick credentials through the standard AWS provider chain, so they are not a third-party path.

Each is a trust path to AWS that does not pass through the GitHub `production` environment (inference). | ✅ (features) / ⚠️ (inference) | [GitHub Actions](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/github-actions/), [AWS credentials](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/credentials) | ### 4.6 What this means for Papaya (inferences — to be used in the design) These are my conclusions from the findings above, not documented facts: 1. **Make "what the reviewer approved" equal "what gets applied", as far as the tools allow.** - **What the PR reviewer sees:** after #2, a PR shows only **non-prod** previews (`pulumi preview --diff` with policies, `sls diff --json` parsed by CI because it always exits 0, 4.4.2). The prod diff differs, because prod has different stack config and state. - **On merge:** `pulumi up` / `package` + `deploy --package` from `main` under `production` (3.6 #1, 4.4.3). Deploy jobs share a concurrency group **without** `cancel-in-progress` (4.1.4). - **Core tension on Team:** with the assumed Team plan (3.7 A1), the merge is the approval for prod, yet **no human sees the prod diff before it is applied**. This should be stated openly to the panel. Options (all ⚠️ design): - (a) **Enterprise:** a prod preview job, then the environment approval, then `up`. The approver sees the prod diff (3.1.1). - (b) **Team:** the deploy workflow on `main` previews prod and **stops automatically** on risky changes: replace or delete of stateful resources, IAM changes, policy violations. Those cases need a second, separate approval path. Safe diffs proceed. This uses `--save-plan` / `up --plan` as a guard only (4.1.3). - (c) A prod-preview identity that cannot write state, for example a Pulumi Cloud stack-read token. Its preview could then be shown on the PR. Unverified whether preview works with read-only access (4.7). - **Staleness:** a PR preview is computed against the base at that time (no merge queue, 3.7). Require branches to be up to date (strict status checks). - **Plan files:** `--save-plan` files can carry secrets if `--show-secrets` is used (4.1.1). 2. **PR previews against prod are not read-only, so do not give PRs prod credentials.** - **State writes:** with an S3 backend, Pulumi needs `PutObject`/`DeleteObject` on `.pulumi/` "across the full stack lifecycle", including preview (4.3.3). PR code running with that role could overwrite or delete prod state. A tampered state makes the next `up` change resources nobody reviewed. - **Secrets:** preview must decrypt stack secrets (KMS decrypt, or Pulumi Cloud stack read access, 4.3.4). `sls diff` resolves `${ssm:…}` with the deploy credentials (4.4.7). - **Code execution:** the program runs as part of preview: "The new desired state is computed by running a Pulumi program" (pulumi preview). Anyone who can open a PR, including an agent, could read prod secrets and state outputs. - **Recommendation:** PRs preview **non-prod stacks only**. The **prod** preview runs after merge, on `main`, in the deploy workflow just before `up`. On Enterprise the environment approval could sit between the two; on Team the merge was the approval (3.6 #1). - Splitting S3 permissions so that preview can write only `locks/` is ⚠️ unverified. The docs list permissions for the whole lifecycle, not per command. - **Roles and trust needed (AWS), each scoped by the `sub` in the repo's format (3.7 A2):** - **non-prod plan/apply:** trusts `pull_request` or non-prod environments. PR code can therefore apply to non-prod, which is acceptable because non-prod holds no real data (GĐ-14); - **prod deploy:** trusts `environment:production` only; - **prod drift check:** a separate read role trusted only from a dedicated `drift` environment restricted to `main`. It must not be able to change state, so state writes stay with the deploy role (⚠️ whether refresh preview needs lock writes, see 4.7). It probably needs `kms:Decrypt`, or Pulumi Cloud stack read, to read state that contains secrets. The drift job can then read prod secrets, which must be noted and restricted. 3. **Close the bypass paths inside the tools:** - **`serverless deploy function`** changes code **and configuration** outside CloudFormation. The change persists after the next deploy (4.4.4). In prod, deny `lambda:UpdateFunctionCode` **and** `lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration` to every principal except the CloudFormation `deploymentRole`. - This works only if `deploymentRole` is set. Otherwise CloudFormation uses the caller's credentials, and the CI role would need those rights itself (4.4.5). - Using `aws:CalledVia` for this is an option (⚠️ untested). - **Least-privilege `deploymentRole`:** it cannot be removed later, and anyone who may operate the stack can use it (4.4.5). Add a `stackPolicy` for stateful resources. - **Pulumi:** prod workflows use an **allowlist** of commands and flags (`preview`, `up` without `--target`, `--target-replace`, `--replace`, `--exclude` or `--skip-preview`). IAM cannot tell `pulumi` commands apart: the deploy role can write state anyway. So keeping state-changing commands (`state …`, `import`, `destroy`, `stack rm`) out of prod runs is enforced only by the workflow allowlist plus CODEOWNERS on `.github/` (3.2.8). Any other use needs a separately approved run. 4. **Policy as code where the agent can't switch it off.** - **Enforcement point:** the policy that counts is the one evaluated during `up` on `main` (4.2.4). - Prefer Pulumi Cloud policy groups (Essentials+) if Papaya is on Pulumi Cloud, and limit who can run `pulumi policy disable`. - Otherwise use `--policy-pack` in a CODEOWNERS-protected reusable workflow (4.2.3). - **No `remediate` level in prod** (4.2.4). - **Serverless:** the CloudFormation template from `sls package` can be checked by a CI policy tool (⚠️ tool not researched). Add IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on changed policies (2.8.1). 5. **Drift is a compliance signal: it means an unreviewed change happened.** - **Pulumi:** scheduled `pulumi refresh --preview-only`, or `pulumi preview --refresh --expect-no-changes`. Without `--refresh`, a preview compares only against recorded state and cannot see drift (4.3.1). Or use Pulumi Cloud drift detection (Pro+), **with auto-remediation off in prod**, because it runs an unreviewed `up` (4.3.2). - **Serverless:** scheduled CloudFormation drift detection, with its coverage limits (4.4.6). It may not catch a `deploy function` code change (⚠️, 4.7). - Every drift finding maps to a CloudTrail actor (2.5) and an incident or ticket. 6. **Third-party credential paths must be closed or put under the same gate** (4.4.9). Pulumi ESC, Pulumi Deployments and Serverless Dashboard Providers each hold a path to prod. - **Default:** do not use them for prod. - **If they are used:** their AWS trust and their admin roles must be as narrow as the GitHub `production` path, and audited (Pulumi Cloud audit logs need Pro+, 4.3.5). 7. **State and secrets:** - **State buckets:** Pulumi state and Serverless state buckets are prod-sensitive stores (encrypted secrets, resource outputs). Restrict them to the deploy roles (4.3.3, 4.4.1). - **Pulumi secrets:** use `awskms` as the secrets provider on a DIY backend (4.3.4). - **Serverless secrets:** resolve them at runtime, not baked into templates (⚠️ 4.4.7). - **Serverless License Key:** keep it in SSM per account, read by the deploy role (≥ 4.4.19). This avoids a long-lived GitHub secret (4.4.8, 3.5.3b). ### 4.7 Open items (Topic 4) - [ ] ⚠️ Papaya's Pulumi backend (Pulumi Cloud vs DIY S3) and edition; Serverless version (≥ 4.37.0 for `diff`?) and subscription. - [ ] ⚠️ Can a CLI user bypass Pulumi Cloud policy-group enforcement? Who may run `pulumi policy disable` (4.2.4)? - [ ] ⚠️ Does `pulumi preview` / `refresh --preview-only` on an S3 backend write only lock objects (4.6 #2)? Read `/docs/iac/operations/stack-management/drift/`. - [ ] ⚠️ Do Serverless-resolved SSM/Secrets Manager values end up in plain text in the CloudFormation template (4.4.7)? - [ ] ⚠️ Does CloudFormation drift detection catch a Lambda code change made by `deploy function` (4.4.6, 4.6 #5)? - [ ] ⚠️ Not covered yet: Pulumi resource options `protect`, `retainOnDelete` and `ignoreChanges` (which hides drift); Pulumi Cloud RBAC; CloudFormation change sets as a review artifact (`deploymentMethod: changesets`); stack termination protection; Serverless `.env` loading. - [ ] ⚠️ Does `pulumi preview` work with read-only stack access (4.6 #1 c)? Does the Pulumi Cloud OIDC policy match the immutable `sub` format assumed in 3.7 A2 (4.1.5)? - [ ] ⚠️ The exact Terraform/OpenTofu command names (4.5); CI policy tools for CloudFormation templates (4.6 #4). ### 4.8 Review log (Topic 4)

**Kết luận:** cả 8 điểm của vòng 2 đã được sửa. Phần sửa sinh ra 1 lỗi MEDIUM mới, ở phương án (c) của 4.6 #1, và 1 điểm LOW nhỏ. Sửa xong (c) thì không còn finding HIGH hay MEDIUM nào.

### Kiểm tra các finding vòng 2

| ID | Trạng thái | Bằng chứng |
|---|---|---|
| N1 | FIXED | 4.6 #1 giờ ghi rõ: PR chỉ hiện preview non-prod, và trên Team "no human sees the prod diff before it is applied". Có các phương án a–c gắn ⚠️, và câu "stop if it differs from the reviewed one" đã bị bỏ. #1 và #2 đã nhất quán. Các tham chiếu 3.7 A1 (Team) và 3.1.1 (required reviewers) đều đúng. |
| L-n1 | FIXED | 4.3.2 giờ là `✅ / ⚠️`. |
| L-n2 | FIXED | 4.6 #3 viết "IAM cannot tell `pulumi` commands apart … enforced only by the workflow allowlist plus CODEOWNERS". |
| L-n3 | FIXED | 4.2.4 đã thêm link Policy as code, là trang chứa quote "fixes the resource automatically" (dòng 49). |
| L-n4 | FIXED | 4.4.9 sửa cách nói về resolvers. Câu này khớp với nguồn "leveraging the standard AWS credential provider chain" (credentials.md:115). |
| L-n5 | FIXED | 4.4.8 có nhãn "Inference:" và marker `✅ / ⚠️`. |

| L-n7 | FIXED | Role drift có nêu `kms:Decrypt` và việc đọc được secret prod. Việc PR apply lên non-prod có lý do theo GĐ-14. |

### Lỗi mới trong text đã sửa

**MEDIUM**

**R3-1. Phương án (c) mở lại một nửa của H1.**
- (c) đề xuất một prod-preview identity "that cannot write state, for example a Pulumi Cloud stack-read token. Its preview could then be shown on the PR."
- Chỉ đọc stack vẫn đủ để giải mã secret của stack (secrets.md:889: keys are obtained "only for users with read access to the stack").
- Preview chạy code của PR (synopsis của `pulumi preview`). Chính 4.6 #2 cũng viết rằng ai mở được PR thì "could read prod secrets and state outputs".
- Như vậy (c) chặn được việc ghi state nhưng vẫn để code PR đọc secret prod và output trong state.
- Fix: thêm vào (c) rằng PR code vẫn đọc được secret prod. Phương án này chỉ chấp nhận được nếu stack prod không có secret, hoặc preview chạy mà không giải mã được secret (⚠️ chưa kiểm tra). Có thể thêm ý này vào mục mới trong 4.7.

**LOW**

**R3-2. 4.4.9: "so they are not a third-party path" là suy luận nhưng chưa gắn nhãn.** Ở cuối row, "(inference)" chỉ gắn cho câu kết luận chung. Gắn nhãn inference cho câu này nữa.

**Tổng: vòng 2 có 8/8 FIXED (0 PARTLY, 0 NOT FIXED). Lỗi mới: HIGH 0 · MEDIUM 1 · LOW 1.**

55:| 4.4.9 | **Other paths that hold prod credentials, outside the GitHub gate:**
- **Pulumi ESC**, recommended by Pulumi for cloud credentials (4.1.4).
- **Pulumi Deployments:** Click to Deploy, schedules, drift runs. They need deployment settings (4.3.2).
- **Serverless Dashboard Providers** ("the easiest and simplest way" to connect to AWS with an IAM role). Credential *resolvers* only pick credentials through the standard AWS provider chain. Inference: so they are not a third-party path.

Each is a trust path to AWS that does not pass through the GitHub `production` environment (inference). | ✅ (features) / ⚠️ (inference) | [GitHub Actions](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/github-actions/), [AWS credentials](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/credentials) | 21: - (c) A prod-preview identity that cannot write state, for example a Pulumi Cloud stack-read 22- token. Its preview could then be shown on the PR. Unverified whether preview works with 23- read-only access (4.7). **Caveat:** stack read access is enough to decrypt the stack's secrets 24: (4.3.4), and preview runs the PR's code. So (c) stops state writes but still lets PR code 25- read prod secrets and outputs (#2). It is acceptable only if the prod stack holds no secrets, 26- or if preview can run without decrypting them (⚠️ unverified, 4.7). 27- - **Staleness:** a PR preview is computed against the base at that time (no merge queue, 3.7). 28- Require branches to be up to date (strict status checks). 29- - **Plan files:** `--save-plan` files can carry secrets if `--show-secrets` is used (4.1.1). 30-2. **PR previews against prod are not read-only, so do not give PRs prod credentials.** -- 150: is applied. After these fixes there are no HIGH/MEDIUM findings: **Topic 4 closed**. 16:- [ ] ⚠️ Does `pulumi preview` work with read-only stack access, and can it run without 17- decrypting stack secrets (4.6 #1 c)? Does the Pulumi 18- Cloud OIDC policy match the immutable `sub` format assumed in 3.7 A2 (4.1.5)? 19-- [ ] ⚠️ The exact Terraform/OpenTofu command names (4.5); CI policy tools for CloudFormation -- 32: - 4.6 #2 called the PR plan role read-only. It can write state and decrypt prod secrets, so 33- PRs now preview non-prod only; 34- - 4.6 #3 must deny `UpdateFunctionConfiguration` too, and depends on `deploymentRole`. 35- - The MEDIUM items: - a command allowlist; - the full set of roles and trust; - CrossGuard rename now ✅. - LOW items: fixed. Gaps: added (4.4.9, 4.6 #6) or moved to 4.7. - **Round 2 (2026-11-08)**, same reviewer: - Round 1: 16 findings FIXED, 2 PARTLY. - New: 0 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM, 7 LOW. - The MEDIUM: 4.6 #1 still described a prod diff on the PR, which contradicted #2. #1 was rewritten. It now states the Team-plan tension openly: no human sees the prod diff before it is applied. Options (a)–(c) are listed for the design. - All 7 LOW items were fixed: the 4.3.2 marker; IAM vs the workflow allowlist; the Policy as code source; resolvers are not a SaaS path; the license-key inference label; the A2 `sub` check; and the drift role reading secrets plus PR code applying to non-prod. - **Round 3 (2026-11-08)**, same reviewer: - Round 2: 8/8 FIXED. - New: 1 MEDIUM, 1 LOW. - The MEDIUM: option (c) would still let PR code read prod secrets. A caveat was added, and the 4.7 item extended. - The LOW: an inference label in 4.4.9. - Both fixed. After these fixes there are no HIGH/MEDIUM findings: **Topic 4 closed**.
